# Data sources

Every number in the report is tagged **PUBLIC DATA** (collected from a public source, listed here) or
**SIMULATED** (generated by `src/simulate.py`, seed 42; assumptions in `data/ASSUMPTIONS.md`).
Simulated numbers are never Tameson's numbers.

Collection rules: robots.txt checked before every request, at least 2.5 s between requests (10 s for product
pages), generic User-Agent, no account, no cart, no checkout, nothing bought. Collected on **14 Nov 2026**.

| File | Source | What | Licence / terms | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data/public/stores.csv` | tameson.com, .co.uk, .nl, .de, .fr, .es, .be (homepages) | Language, currency and market of each country store (Shopify Markets fields in the page) | Public web pages, facts only | 2026-11-14 |

| Job posting | himalayas.app (Tameson, Marketing Analytics Specialist, Paid Acquisition) | Stack and recent work quoted in the report (Markov MTA, cohort LTV in bidding, BigQuery + Looker Studio, CAC / POAS / LTV) | Public job ad | posted ~2026-10-29 |

Notes
- The GA4 sample is **not Tameson's data**: it is the only public set of real GA4 user journeys. It is used to
  show the method (attribution with intervals) on real paths and to size A/B tests on a real conversion rate.
- Google Trends topics: "Pneumatics" is ambiguous in Spanish and French (neumático / pneumatique also mean tyre)
  and "Pneumatic cylinder" is too sparse at weekly level: both are left out of seasonality and country priority.
- Shopify's storefront JSON endpoints are limited on this site (collections return one product), so prices come
  from product pages. The first "price" field on a product page is Shopify's product JSON, in cents; prices are
  divided by 100 (checked: all captured values are integers; e.g. a stainless G1/4 solenoid valve = $333.12).
- With BigQuery access, `sql/bigquery/ga4_markov_paths.sql` rebuilds the path table from the official source.

## SIMULATED

`src/simulate.py` (seed 42): weekly spend per channel and country, every order with its margin, B2B customers and
their repeat orders, one geo holdout. Calibrated on the public data above (countries, categories, list prices,
Google Trends seasonality); all other inputs are assumptions listed in `data/ASSUMPTIONS.md`.
